khai.tagline: Decay as process: the material entropy a place or a thing undergoes -- matter losing the order imposed on it whether or not it is used, rust and rot and crumble working the fabric from within, and the surface aged into patina, read as loss or as the value of age.

card.wire: Attaches at Place on the Shown chapter, and at Piece on the Apparent chapter -- one phenomenon (material entropy) on two types, the first engine to wire multiple cargo types, because rust is rust on a rail or a blade. The root (process_decay.md) declares decay as the slow loss of the order a maker imposed on matter: metal, wood, and stone giving themselves back to oxide, rot, and grit once the making stops holding them, borne in the fabric of a place or the material of a thing and shown before anyone names it. It reads the use-independent material process only; on a place it hands off the setting (space's), the atmospheric load (weather's), the surface worn from outside (erosion's), and the owner's withdrawal (dereliction's); on an object it hands off the degradation of use (wear's -- decay is what takes the unused thing, wear what the used one spends).
card.issue: Four modes over an entropy root, each working its own material. Rust is metal returning to oxide, the iron bleeding orange and losing its strength from within. Rot is organic matter breaking down, wood softening and fabric perishing under damp and fungus. Crumble is mineral fabric disintegrating, stone spalling and masonry returning to grit. Patina is the twist: slow, even, benign decay laid down as a surface that reads not as loss but as time made visible and prized -- the age-value a restoration must choose to keep or erase.
card.require: Two altitudes hold the engine. The law: declared once in the project's Instructions Knowledge chapter, linking the root, so decay reads system-wide and no matter escapes it. The link: a place carries under Shown, or an object under Apparent, the mode of decay it shows, linking one of the four.
card.enforce: Structure is checked; the read is judged. The kit verifies the law is declared and each decaying place or object links a real mode file under Shown or Apparent. Whether the mode is true to the material and the age is semantic, taught and reviewed, never failed by the suite. The place or thing shows the decay; it enacts the loss, it does not narrate it, and it never stands in for a persona's feeling.
card.setup: Declare the law in the Instructions Knowledge chapter, linking the root. Then give each decaying thing its read -- a place under Shown, an object under Apparent: the mode its fabric or material shows -- the rust on the metal, the rot in the wood, the crumble of the stone, or the patina prized on the surface. Keep it use-independent material entropy -- the fall the matter takes whether or not anyone touches it -- and hand the atmospheric load to weather, the worn-from-outside surface to erosion, the owner's withdrawal to dereliction, the degradation of use to wear, and the intervention that arrests it to reclamation (on a place) or restoration (on an object). Read patina as value, not only loss: decay is ambivalent, and the same process that ruins one thing enriches another.
